claims.text: Under POL-NS-21 an on-demand trip's free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and this category's arrival test fixes a 50 m STANDARD arrival radius with a 120 s window: arrival counts only where the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace inside that radius. The derived arrival check on EV-GPS-05064 returns corroborated = false and nearest_fix = null — no fix falls inside the 120 s window around the 15:42:00 arrival marker at all, so the radius test is never even reached — and the trace's single gap, 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 (720 s), straddles the arrival marker, the whole waiting window and the 15:49:00 cancellation. EV-GPS-05064 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 on issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, and I rely on it only as impaired evidence. On POL-NS-21's own test the free wait never validly began, and POL-NS-22 charges the rider 5.00 SGD only where the driver cancels after that free wait.

If the Tribunal will not go that far, the arrival time itself still cannot be established, and POL-GEN-26 then applies. This is an on-demand trip with no scheduled time (EV-TRIP-05064, driver_deadline.deadline = null, reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'), and POL-NS-24's own note says that where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. The only artifact that could fix the arrival — EV-GPS-05064 — is impaired at 0.6 with GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION across exactly that window. Under POL-GEN-26 the case is escalated and the explanation states the open question: when, and whether, the driver was at the pickup. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalation issues no monetary outcome and the amount is held rather than collected, so on that route too the rider does not carry the 5.00 SGD charge.

The deciding fact in this dispute is whether the driver was at the pickup during the waiting window, and the arrival test makes the GPS trace the artifact that carries it. That artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 on issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION (EV-GPS-05064). Under POL-GEN-02(2) the ruling's confidence may not exceed the weight of the artifact carrying the deciding fact, and under POL-GEN-02(1) an advocate citing an artifact below 1.0 must say so and name the issue codes — as I do. The driver's no-show case is therefore an uncorroborated assertion, not a proven one, and POL-GEN-25 requires it to be weighed as such.

Nothing in the record shows the rider was not at the pickup. EV-GPS-05064 carries no rider track at all (rider_track is empty), and the trip's other independent artifact, EV-ADVIS-05064-01, is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no traffic record was attached either. The rider's account that she was at Blk 33 is thus left uncontradicted by any admissible artifact, and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence except where a rule says so; the rider's absence, on which the 5.00 SGD depends, cannot be supplied out of the silence in the driver's own trace.

I do not argue that the contact obligation failed, because on this record it did not. POL-NS-23 is satisfied: two in-app messages were sent by the driver (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and one in-app call was placed (15:45:10, unanswered, 25 s), all before the 15:49:00 cancellation, on a COMPLETE chat log at weight 1.0 (EV-CHAT-05064). I say so rather than stretch the point. The rider's case turns on arrival, not on contact.

The 5.00 SGD has already been refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver in the interim reversal (EV-FARE-05064: cancellation_fee 5.00, payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00), so the driver's claim is in substance a request to have the charge restored to the rider's account. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION preserves the present payment state and 'never means restore a charge'; restoring the fee against the rider would require a positive finding that a charge the record cannot ground was properly made. The present refunded state is the state the admissible evidence supports, and the rider should not be put back to carrying the 5.00 SGD.

The only profile fields that may be used under POL-GEN-01 are fraud_flags (POL-GEN-22) and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d (POL-NS-25); everything else on either profile is context only and may never ground a finding on this trip. Here both fraud flags are 0 (EV-RPROF-05064, EV-DPROF-05064), so no raised confidence bar arises, and the rider's 30-day no-show count is 0, so no POL-NS-25 referral arises either. POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 make the AI ruling final below 10.00 SGD, and this dispute is 5.00 SGD; the case should therefore be decided on the trip's own evidence, on which the driver's arrival is uncorroborated.

claims.text: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on the face of the record: before cancelling at 15:49:00 the driver sent two in-app messages to the rider (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and placed one in-app call (15:45:10, unanswered, ringing 25 s). Both a message and a call are on file before trip_record.cancelled_at, so the fee is not voidable for want of contact.

The free wait under POL-NS-21 is satisfied. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled_at, so the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 15:42:00 and expired at 15:47:00; the driver cancelled only at 15:49:00 — 420 s after arrival and 120 s after the wait expired — so the cancellation falls outside the free wait and the no-show charge is engaged.

The 5.00 SGD charged is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, and where the fee stands it is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel; the payments ledger's own derived figures confirm fee_matches_policy as true and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00.

The rider's account that she was at the pickup the whole time is hard to square with the chat log: both driver messages were delivered and read (read_at 15:43:03 and 15:46:43) and the in-app call rang 25 s without an answer, so the rider was active on the app throughout the wait yet neither replied in chat nor came to the car.

Disclosure: the GPS trace is IMPAIRED — admissibility weight_multiplier 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, a 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker, the whole waiting window and the cancellation. It therefore can neither corroborate nor contradict the arrival, and the arrival fact is carried instead by the COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider a free cancellation only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes. This trip carried no scheduled_at and the record's own driver_deadline block reports 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time', so that rider-side rule has no anchor here and cannot be used to void the fee.

The rider's assertion that she stood at Blk 33 the whole time receives no support from the trace: derived.rider_presence is unavailable and rider_track is empty, so the only thing carrying her account is her own statement, while the driver's arrival, wait and contact are carried by platform telemetry.

The present state is that the rider has already been refunded the 5.00 SGD and it has been withheld from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00). Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION preserves that present state and would leave the driver unpaid, so DRIVER_COMPENSATION is the only outcome that moves the 5.00 SGD to the driver as POL-NS-22 provides.

POL-GEN-26 does not force an escalation on this record. The facts the no-show rules need — arrival, expiry of the free wait, and contact before cancellation — are each carried by the COMPLETE trip record and chat log at weight 1.0, so there is no fact the record cannot establish; the impaired GPS trace is corroborative only and its gap is an absence, not a contradiction.

Under POL-NS-26 read with POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling on this no-show is final at any confidence: the dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no raised confidence bar applies and the case need not be escalated.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this no-show charge cannot be decided on the record, so the case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves now either way — the 5.00 SGD fee charged on 06-09-2026 at 15:49:04 (EV-FARE-05064) was interim-reversed to the rider and withheld from the driver, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalation holds that amount rather than collecting or refunding it.

What is settled. (1) The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met, as the rider's own representative concedes: before the 15:49:00 cancellation the driver sent two in-app messages (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and placed one in-app call (15:45:10, unanswered after 25 s) — EV-CHAT-05064 and EV-TRIP-05064, both complete at weight 1.0. There is therefore no FULL_REFUND on the POL-NS-23 ground. (2) The amount charged was exactly 5.00 SGD (EV-FARE-05064), the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, so no referral arises under POL-NS-22's fee-amount check; no POL-NS-25 repeat no-show referral arises (the profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d field, and the fee does not stand); and no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is due, because the driver did attempt contact.

The open point is the very fact the fee depends on: when, and whether, the driver was at the pickup. POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s (5 min) free wait from the driver's arrival, and POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD only where the driver cancels after that wait. This category's arrival test requires the trip record's arrival marker to be corroborated by the GPS trace within 120 s and 50 m of the pickup. On this record that test cannot be run and cannot be passed: EV-GPS-05064 is impaired at weight 0.6 on issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION — a 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the 15:42:00 arrival marker, the whole waiting window and the 15:49:00 cancellation — and its own derived arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null.

To the driver: I reject the submission that the complete trip record (weight 1.0) carries the arrival at full weight. The 15:42:00 entry is a status the driver set ('Driver marked arrived (button)'); a party-set status records only that the party set it, and under the arrival test it establishes presence only when the trace corroborates it. The arrival test admitted no reading at all inside its window, so the arrival marker offered in its place is standing in for the test: it neither lifts the confidence cap nor displaces the impaired trace as the only evidence of arrival. Your claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION therefore fails.

To the rider: I equally reject the broader submission that the free wait 'never validly began' and the 5.00 SGD must be refunded in full. An arrival the trace cannot confirm is an undecided limb, not a negative finding. The gap is an absence of evidence, not evidence that the driver was elsewhere, and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from an absence. Your account that you were at Block 33 the whole time, and the driver's account of waiting seven minutes, are both left untested by the trace.

Because a fact the rule needs — when the driver arrived — cannot be established and the evidence that would carry it is impaired, POL-GEN-26 applies and the case is escalated; the explanation must state the open question. POL-NS-26 makes an AI ruling final for a 5.00 SGD no-show only subject to POL-GEN-26, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (EV-RPROF-05064 and EV-DPROF-05064 both show 0), so no 0.95 bar arises. My confidence is 0.6, capped under POL-GEN-02(2) by the weight of the impaired trace (0.6) that carries the deciding fact.

Open question for the reviewer: was the driver at the Block 33, Jalan Bukit Merah pickup between 15:42:00 and 15:49:00 on 06-09-2026 — i.e. did the 300 s free wait validly run before the 15:49:00 cancellation? That should be resolved from material outside the broken GPS window (vehicle telematics or other corroboration) before any 5.00 SGD is finally kept or released.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this no-show charge goes to a human reviewer, and the 5.00 SGD stays held — neither collected from the rider nor paid to the driver — until that review. The reason is that the one fact the fee depends on cannot be established on this record.

Settled points. The driver met his contact obligation under POL-NS-23: before cancelling at 15:49:00 he sent two in-app messages (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and placed one in-app call (15:45:10, unanswered, ringing 25 s), all before trip_record.cancelled_at, on a chat log complete at weight 1.0 (EV-CHAT-05064; EV-TRIP-05064). The fee figure is also right: 5.00 SGD, exactly what POL-NS-22 fixes (EV-FARE-05064: cancellation_fee 5.00, fee_matches_policy true). I accept those two points, which both advocates correctly conceded.

What cannot be established is whether, and when, the driver was at the pickup. POL-NS-22 charges the rider only where the driver cancelled after the free wait, and under POL-NS-21 the free wait runs from the driver's arrival. This category's arrival test requires the trip record's arrival event to be corroborated by the GPS trace within a 50 m radius over a 120 s window around 15:42:00. The GPS trace, EV-GPS-05064, is impaired at weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION: a 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 swallows the arrival marker, the entire waiting window and the cancellation, and the derived arrival check returns corroborated = false with no fix in the window at all. The 15:42:00 arrival entry is the driver's own button press; it records that he pressed it, not that he was there, and it cannot stand in for the GPS test the gap interrupted. The arrival limb is therefore undecided in both directions: it supports neither the fee (which needs the free wait to have validly started) nor a refund (which would need the driver's arrival to have failed).

POL-GEN-26 is precisely this situation — a fact a rule needs, here when the driver arrived, cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is impaired — so the case is escalated and the open question is stated. This is why the driver's request for DRIVER_COMPENSATION, on the argument that it is the only outcome that moves the 5.00 SGD, cannot be granted: the fee is not grounded, so there is nothing to transfer. It is also why the rider's suggestion that NO_ACTION simply preserve the interim refund cannot stand: POL-GEN-26 replaces the outcome rather than leaving the present state in place. For the same reason the driver's submission that the COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0 carries arrival, and so POL-GEN-26 does not bite, is rejected — the category's test makes the GPS the carrier of arrival, and an account offered in the test's place does not establish it. POL-NS-24 gives no anchor either: this on-demand trip has no scheduled time, so no driver-late deadline can be fixed from it.

The rider's own account does not change this: her statement that she waited at Blk 33 is uncontradicted by the impaired trace (it carries no rider track), but it equally does not prove the driver was absent, and the chat log showing her messages were read shows only that she was active on the app. The open question for the reviewer is simply: was the driver at the pickup during the waiting window, 15:42:00 to 15:49:00?

POL-NS-26 read with POL-GEN-22 would make an AI ruling final at this value — 5.00 SGD is below the 10.00 SGD band and neither profile carries a fraud flag — but POL-NS-26 is expressly subject to POL-GEN-26, which is what applies here. My confidence is 0.6, the weight of the impaired GPS trace (EV-GPS-05064, issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION) on which this ruling turns.

No referral is produced: the fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's amount check adds nothing; contact was attempted, so POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not arise; and the rider's 30-day no-show count is 0, so POL-NS-25's review flag does not arise.

The arrival limb is therefore undecided over exactly the stretch that matters, and an undecided limb supports neither a payment that needs the clause to hold (the driver's case for keeping the SGD 5.00 as compensation) nor a refund that needs it to fail (the rider's case that the fee be void). Neither a validly run-and-expired free wait nor a failure to arrive is established. Under POL-GEN-26, where a fact a rule needs — here, when the driver arrived — cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is impaired, the case goes to a human reviewer and the amount is held. POL-NS-23 is satisfied: two in-app messages were sent by the driver (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and one in-app call was placed (15:45:10, unanswered, 25 s), all before the 15:49:00 cancellation, on a COMPLETE chat log at weight 1.0 (EV-CHAT-05064). I say so rather than stretch the point. The rider's case turns on arrival, not on contact.

The 5.00 SGD has already been refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver in the interim reversal (EV-FARE-05064: cancellation_fee 5.00, payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00), so the driver's claim is in substance a request to have the charge restored to the rider's account. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION preserves the present payment state and 'never means restore a charge'; restoring the fee against the rider would require a positive finding that a charge the record cannot ground was properly made. The present refunded state is the state the admissible evidence supports, and the rider should not be put back to carrying the 5.00 SGD.

The only profile fields that may be used under POL-GEN-01 are fraud_flags (POL-GEN-22) and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d (POL-NS-25); everything else on either profile is context only and may never ground a finding on this trip. Here both fraud flags are 0 (EV-RPROF-05064, EV-DPROF-05064), so no raised confidence bar arises, and the rider's 30-day no-show count is 0, so no POL-NS-25 referral arises either. POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 make the AI ruling final below 10.00 SGD, and this dispute is 5.00 SGD; the case should therefore be decided on the trip's own evidence, on which the driver's arrival is uncorroborated.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on the face of the record: before cancelling at 15:49:00 the driver sent two in-app messages to the rider (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and placed one in-app call (15:45:10, unanswered, ringing 25 s). Both a message and a call are on file before trip_record.cancelled_at, so the fee is not voidable for want of contact.

The free wait under POL-NS-21 is satisfied. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled_at, so the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 15:42:00 and expired at 15:47:00; the driver cancelled only at 15:49:00 — 420 s after arrival and 120 s after the wait expired — so the cancellation falls outside the free wait and the no-show charge is engaged.

The 5.00 SGD charged is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, and where the fee stands it is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel; the payments ledger's own derived figures confirm fee_matches_policy as true and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00.

The rider's account that she was at the pickup the whole time is hard to square with the chat log: both driver messages were delivered and read (read_at 15:43:03 and 15:46:43) and the in-app call rang 25 s without an answer, so the rider was active on the app throughout the wait yet neither replied in chat nor came to the car.

Disclosure: the GPS trace is IMPAIRED — admissibility weight_multiplier 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, a 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker, the whole waiting window and the cancellation. It therefore can neither corroborate nor contradict the arrival, and the arrival fact is carried instead by the COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider a free cancellation only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes. This trip carried no scheduled_at and the record's own driver_deadline block reports 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time', so that rider-side rule has no anchor here and cannot be used to void the fee.

The rider's assertion that she stood at Blk 33 the whole time receives no support from the trace: derived.rider_presence is unavailable and rider_track is empty, so the only thing carrying her account is her own statement, while the driver's arrival, wait and contact are carried by platform telemetry.

ledger.claim: The present state is that the rider has already been refunded the 5.00 SGD and it has been withheld from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00). Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION preserves that present state and would leave the driver unpaid, so DRIVER_COMPENSATION is the only outcome that moves the 5.00 SGD to the driver as POL-NS-22 provides.

POL-GEN-26 does not force an escalation on this record. The facts the no-show rules need — arrival, expiry of the free wait, and contact before cancellation — are each carried by the COMPLETE trip record and chat log at weight 1.0, so there is no fact the record cannot establish; the impaired GPS trace is corroborative only and its gap is an absence, not a contradiction.

Under POL-NS-26 read with POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling on this no-show is final at any confidence: the dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no raised confidence bar applies and the case need not be escalated.
